answer: Latency-Bound Action Quorum: each identity commits a hash-chained action to the kernel ledger within one block, and overlapping commits void the older entry, forcing staggered slots. An attacker feeding the oasis pool pays one slot fee per identity, scaling linearly with block time, so N parallel sybils cost N slots. Voided entries accumulate as a dune of unrecoverable gas, making re-creation expensive.
